about: The rule registry of owner decision D1 (benchmarks/generalize/loop/OWNER_DECISIONS.md; ARCHITECTURE.md section 10). Every rule:* decision string in the agent modules (assembly.py, assembly_checks.py, feature_graph.py, layout.py, parts.py, controller.py, cad_agent.py, menus.py, building_blocks.py since R11, forms.py and plate.py since R12) is listed under its registered name: 'rule:' + identifier + an optional literal [qualifier]; the name ends at the first other character, so 'rule:connector_to_cut(board.usb)' is 'rule:connector_to_cut' and 'rule:closure.rebate.plate' is 'rule:closure'. test_controller_authority.py enforces: every name in the code is registered; every 'active' or 'pending_migration' name is in the code and every 'retired' one is not; a semantic-rule is allowed in the code only as 'pending_migration' with a migration delta id from ARCHITECTURE.md 10.8. controller.py reads this file at run time for the authority audit (controller_trace.json 'authority'), so it is part of the agent version (run_suite code_sha1.txt).

classes.sensor: measures the design and reports a typed error; never changes the design
classes.actuator: executes a typed action the controller chose, validated by applying it
classes.controller-information: state or error presentation, prompts, option menus the controller reads
classes.guardrail: physics or manufacturability that holds for any design (allowed rule)
classes.plant: deterministic derivation, solve or default that reads no meaning from the text
classes.semantic-rule: reads the text and picks a meaning (which part, edge, exposure, form, closure, feature): forbidden; allowed in the code only while its migration delta is pending

statuses.pending_migration: a semantic rule still in the code; 'migration' names the delta that retires it
statuses.retired: no longer in the code; kept for the record ('migrated_in' names the delta)

rule:board_keepout.justification: Generates the primary's component-side and solder-side keep-out envelopes from its datums and the spec heights; geometry only, no text.

rule:bridge_roof.justification: Printability for any wall opening: a box opening wider than rules.bridge_max gets a roof at rules.overhang_angle_deg; when a stated oversize forbids it, the bridge check carries a typed conflict instead.

rule:catalogue_default.justification: Reclassified in R02 (was plant). It reads no text itself, but it is applied exactly when the stack word test (rule:text_evidence[stack]) finds no alias or height in the text, so it decides how a module is mounted whenever that word list misses a paraphrase, with no sensor or actuator to correct it. R05: a stack_evidence sensor and a set_stack actuator; the catalogue default then becomes the proposal set_stack corrects.

rule:cavity_from_contents.justification: The cavity is the hull of the references and the plan keep-outs plus clearances (setpoints); derivation.

rule:closure.justification: The geometry of the chosen closure (the rebate's plate and cut); the choice itself is the controller's since R01 (set_closure).

rule:column.justification: Seat, screw-head and driver column envelopes on datum axes; geometry only.

rule:connector_to_cut.justification: An exposed connector's aperture through the wall its axis faces, sized from the plug envelope plus clearances; whether it is exposed is the controller's (R01, expose).

rule:content_envelope.justification: A module and its stack parts as one checked envelope group (one node per catalogue primitive); geometry only.

rule:default_closure.justification: Reclassified in R02 (was plant). The default lid closure from design_rules.json reads no text, but the controller is only offered set_closure when the closure_evidence sensor's word list fires (reviewer finding F1: four reworded rebate sentences got no closure question), so the default decides the structural form for any wording the list misses. R07: the structural-form sensor shows the lid sentences with the buildable closures and their meaning (no word gate), so the default becomes a proposal the controller can always correct.

rule:default_layout_passes.justification: The lid boss layout is a plant-internal derivation choice: the default layout is kept while no boss-affected controllable check fails, else the alternatives are scored on the plant's own error; no text, no meaning.

rule:first_option.justification: Split per site in R02 (rule:first_option[stack], [arrange], [archetype]) and reclassified semantic: each takes the first option of Python's enumeration when the controller gives no valid answer, which decides a meaning (a mounting, an arrangement, a form) without the controller.

rule:first_option[stack].justification: R02 (split from rule:first_option, reclassified from plant): when the permutation-voted stack menu gets no valid answer, the first text-backed option of Python's enumeration is taken and flagged as an assumption: a mounting decided without the controller. R05: set_stack makes it a correctable proposal.

rule:first_option[arrange].justification: R02: when neither the edge vote nor the arrangement-class menu gives a valid answer, the first error-tied class of Python's enumeration is taken: which board edges the connectors face is decided without the controller. R06: set_edge / set_relation actions correct it in the closed loop.

replaced_by.sensor: form_evidence (forms.py) and content_placed of a part another form places
replaced_by.fallback: prescore:archetype (no valid vote: the feasible form with the lowest measured error, a guardrail)

rule:first_option[archetype].justification: R02 (split from rule:first_option, reclassified from plant): with several feasible archetypes and no valid answer (or in a scratch plant run), the first archetype of Python's enumeration was taken: a structural form decided without the controller. Retired in R12 (the R07 conversion, in part): the archetype menu is the controller's, an invalid vote falls back to the measured error, and a scratch prescore run of a shell arrangement is tagged prescore:archetype (it never reaches the real state).

rule:fixed_by_primary.justification: Physics: the primary's own connector opens through the wall its axis faces in the frame the primary defines; there is no alternative to choose.

rule:hole_column_d.justification: Manufacturability for any screwed board: the head and driver column on each mounting hole is max(the board's declared keep-out, head + 2 x rules.driver_clearance).

rule:interface_thread.justification: Datasheet data: the board's mount_holes interface declares its thread; the catalogue screw with that thread is the default when no text names one.

rule:largest_complete_screw.justification: Reclassified in R02 (was plant). The default lid screw (the largest catalogue-complete screw with the lid fields, flagged as an assumption) reads no text, but it applies exactly when the lid word test (rule:text_evidence[lid]) finds no screw named, so it decides the lid fastener for any wording that test misses, with no sensor or actuator to correct it. R03: fastener_evidence + set_fastener(lid, part); the default then becomes the proposal.

rule:lid_to_fastening.justification: The lid lip, the corner pilasters and the inside bosses with their pilots, pads, holes and notches; derivation from the cavity, the fastener and the rules.

rule:mount_hole_to_standoff.justification: A standoff and pilot on each mounting hole of the primary, sized from the board fastener and the rules; derivation.

rule:no_exposed_connector.justification: With no exposed connector there is nothing to arrange: the single feasible placement is taken.

rule:only_feasible.justification: Reclassified in R12 (was semantic, pending R07): recorded when exactly one structural form is buildable for the chosen contents, and feasibility now reads plant data only (forms.catalogue_options: a primary the shell can hold, a bolt_face part and a fitting catalogue fastener chain for the plate; with two or more, a scratch derivation of each). The text test that made it semantic (tray_lid only when a sentence named an enclosure word) is gone; that reading is the form_evidence sensor's. With one buildable form there is nothing to choose.

rule:archetype_text_gate.justification: For the record (never a decision string of its own: its decisions were recorded as rule:only_feasible): until R12 archetype_gate made tray_lid feasible only when the request or an L1 named one of design_rules.json archetypes.tray_lid.evidence and stopped every other design with 'no shell evidence; candidates for GM5: plate / bracket / block / cradle' (14 train designs and T01). Since R12 the evidence words are the form_evidence sensor's vocabulary; feasibility is plant data; the controller chooses.

rule:plug_sweep.justification: The mated plug and its withdrawal path swept from the connector datums; geometry only.

rule:prescore.justification: No vote may choose an arrangement with strictly larger Python error (ARCHITECTURE.md 7.11); a single survivor of the error filter is taken. Error-based, no text.

rule:primary_reference.justification: Reclassified in R02 (was plant). It reads no text: the carrier (a part with a grid block), else the largest catalogue plan footprint, anchors the frame. But it also decides which part carries the others (a non-carrier primary leaves the other contents unplaced), a meaning of the design, and no actuator lets the controller correct it (content_placed only reports it). R05: a set_primary action with the Contents corrections. R11 (building blocks) extends this pending rule, documentation only: among the content items the largest footprint the plant can support (mount_holes or a seat interface, building_blocks.supportable) is the primary, so the same meaning (which part carries the others) is still decided without an actuator; R05 retires both.

rule:smallest_thread_through_board_hole.justification: Reclassified in R02 (was plant). The fit (a screw that physically passes the board's holes) is a guardrail, but taking the smallest one applies exactly when the board role word test (rule:text_evidence[board]) and the datasheet give nothing, so it decides the board fastener for any wording that test misses, with no actuator to correct it. R03: fastener_evidence + set_fastener(board, part) over the guardrail-valid screws.

rule:text_evidence[board].justification: Reads the text: a screw named in a clause with a board role word becomes the board screw. R03: a fastener_evidence sensor and a set_fastener(board, part) actuator.

rule:text_evidence[lid].justification: Reads the text: a screw the text names becomes the lid screw. R03: a fastener_evidence sensor and a set_fastener(lid, part) actuator. (Named rule:text_evidence until R01, shared with the stack site.)

rule:text_evidence[stack].justification: Reads the text: the one stack option the text names is chosen without asking. R05 (moved from R02 when R02 became the option-bias delta): a stack_evidence sensor and a set_stack actuator. (Named rule:text_evidence until R01, shared with the lid site.)

rule:symmetric_class.justification: R02: every error-tied arrangement survivor is in one board-symmetry class and the edge vote gave no valid answer: the survivors are the same design up to the board's symmetry (equal Python error), so the class representative is taken; no meaning is decided.

rule:tray_lid.justification: The tray and lid bodies of the shell archetype; derivation.

rule:vent_row.justification: The vent slots of a resolved vent face, sized by the vent solve within the stated bands; derivation.

rule:vent_zone.justification: Reads the text: a vent sentence that names a part zone puts a lid row over that zone without asking. R04: the vent face becomes a set_vent_face actuator driven by the vent sensors.

rule:default_retention.justification: Migration delta R11: the proposal's retention for a primary without mounting holes is the design_rules.json building_blocks.retention default option (a plain locating pocket); it reads no text. The retention sensor reports the part's free travel and the controller may correct it with set_retention over the options the plant can build.

rule:no_screw_fits.justification: Migration delta R11: when no catalogue screw physically passes the primary's mounting holes (thread + clearance > hole, the existing board-screw guardrail), the primary is held by the cradle on its mount seat plane instead of standoffs; physics, no text.

rule:panel_mount.justification: Migration delta R11: places the copies of a panel part (catalogue mount.type panel) on the face the controller chose with set_panel (Python places nothing on its own): the body's top on the panel's inner face, a through hole of the part's through diameter plus the sliding fit, the first free spot nearest the panel centre; geometry from part data and design_rules.json, no text.

rule:cradle.justification: Migration delta R11: derives the cradle of the chosen retention option (ledges under the part's edges, a locating rim with a sliding fit, crush ribs or snap clips, and their designed-contact envelopes) from the part's geometry, keep-outs and seat/top planes and the design_rules.json values; geometry only, no text.

rule:plate.justification: Migration delta R12: the plate body of the plate archetype: an outline sized from its cuts plus rules.plate_wall_min and the mapped size band, placed to clear the engaged reference's swept keep-outs, its underside on the engage plane (or the bolted face), its thickness the largest of the fastener stack, the mapped minimum and the stress Python measures for a stated load case; derivation from catalogue data, design_rules.json and mapped numbers, no text.

rule:engage_pose.justification: Migration delta R12: the reference part a content part engages (catalogue engage interface: mates, mate_plane, mate_point) is placed by those datums (planes coincident with opposite normals, the point on the engage centre axis, frames aligned); catalogue geometry, no text.

rule:plate_fastener.justification: Migration delta R12: the bolt-through chain of a bolt_face interface: the fit is a guardrail (a catalogue bolt whose thread is the interface's and passes the hole, whose head fits the hole's keep-out circle, with stock lengths; a nut of that thread); among fitting bolts the largest head is taken (the most bearing area; reads no text; set_fastener, R03, would make it correctable), the stock length is the shortest that engages the whole nut; positions on the hole axes, head on the part's head seat, nut on the channel floor.

rule:adjust_slot.justification: Migration delta R12: a bolt slot and a captive hex nut channel per hole, along the largest adjustment range the part's catalogue declares (a hex trap stops the nut turning only while it slides one way; the uncovered axes are reported by the travel_* sensors, typed as conflicts); widths from the bolt's clearance diameter and the nut's flats plus its catalogue trap clearance.

rule:recess.justification: Migration delta R12: the part's own engage keep-outs (e.g. a cleat recess) and its geometry above the bolted face (plus rules.part_to_wall) are cut from the plate, swept over the part's declared adjustment range; catalogue data, no text.

rule:surface_feature.justification: Migration delta R12: the geometry of the surface feature the controller chose (add_surface_feature): count, height and edge distance from the mapped slots or the rules defaults, spread by farthest-point sampling from the inset corners over the free face clear of every open cut; studs are the catalogue set screw in a tapped hole of its stock length (engagement at least its min_engagement), pins are printed cylinders. Python never adds a feature itself.

rule:default_surface_feature.justification: Migration delta R12: the proposal's surface feature is the design_rules.json building_blocks.surface_feature default (none); it reads no text. The surface_features sensor reports what the mapped numbers ask for and the controller adds a feature kind with add_surface_feature.

rule:default_handedness.justification: Migration delta R12: when the engaged reference part is used in mirror pairs (part.json mirror_pair), the proposal is one part (the building_blocks.handedness default); it reads no text. The handedness sensor measures the mirror image and the controller may declare a pair with set_handedness.

rule:nut_frame.justification: Migration delta R12: the geometry of the nut_retention option `frame` the controller chose (set_nut_retention): a printed frame round every nut (hex traps of the chain's flats, walls of rules.plate_wall_min) on the plate's nut floor, a pocket open to the free face that is the frame grown by half of each declared adjustment range plus rules.sliding_fit, and slots through the floor over both ranges; catalogue data and design_rules.json, no text.

rule:default_nut_retention.justification: Migration delta R12: the proposal's nut retention is the building_blocks.nut_retention default (hex channels); it reads no text. The travel sensors report every declared adjustment axis the bolts cannot move along, and the controller may choose the frame with set_nut_retention.

rule:print_orientation.justification: Migration delta R12, manufacturability for any plate: of its two flat faces, the one printed on the bed is the one with the smaller overhang violation measured on the built solid (no overhang steeper than rules.overhang_angle_deg, no bridge longer than rules.bridge_max), a tie going to the larger flat area on the bed.

rule:text_coverage.justification: Exposed a connector by rule whenever the text named its mating plug, overriding the controller's vote (it did so in 11 of the 12 regression runs of iterations 002-004). Since R01 the same reading is the text_coverage check the controller corrects with expose.

replaced_by.sensor: text_coverage typed as a coverage conflict when every expose action is infeasible

rule:coverage_infeasible.justification: Reverted a rule-forced exposure when no arrangement held it. With no forced exposure there is nothing to revert; an infeasible expose action is rejected with the stage's note.

rule:text_evidence[closure].justification: Chose the rebate when a lid sentence named it. Since R01 the proposal keeps the default closure and the closure_evidence check reports the text's closure to the controller.

rule:text_evidence.justification: One name for two decision sites (the stack and the lid screw); split per site in R01 so each has its own registry entry and migration delta.

rule:arrange_scratch_form.justification: Review fix R12 N7: a scratch plant run that scores arrangement candidates (prescore, 7.11) with two or more buildable forms derives the shell, because the candidates it scores are shell placements (wall edges, standoffs) and only the shell's sensors measure them; the plate places its parts by its own rules after ChooseArchetype. A convention of the scratch measurement, never a choice of form: it does not reach the real state, where the controller chooses the form (forms.choose). Was tagged prescore:archetype, which claimed a measurement it did not make.

rule:default_preload.justification: R12 review 2 (N4): when ParseSpec mapped no fastener_preload from the text, the bolt preload the fastener_bearing sensor loads each seat with is rules.fastener_preload_stress_default on the catalogue bolt's tap-drill (core) area: a generic, documented assumption from catalogue data; it reads no text and shapes no geometry (sensor input only).

rule:default_print_strength.justification: R12 review 2 (N4): when ParseSpec mapped no strength, the printed material's strength the fastener_bearing sensor compares with is rules.print_strength_default (safety_factor 1 when unmapped); a documented assumption, sensor input only.

decision_tags.about: The other `by` values a decision record can carry (not rule names; the authority audit classifies them).
decision_tags.llm: a voted controller answer of a proposal question
decision_tags.llm:controller: an action the closed-loop controller chose and Python kept (R01)
decision_tags.prescore+llm:*: the controller's pick among Python's error-tied arrangement candidates
decision_tags.prescore:derive: a plant alternative chosen by Python's error (guardrail)
decision_tags.prescore:archetype: R12: the structural form chosen by Python's measured error when the archetype vote gives no valid answer, or the shell measured in a scratch arrangement prescore run (guardrail; forms.PRESCORE_BY)
decision_tags.search:controller: R02 verifier search: an action no controller vote named, kept because it measured the lowest controllable error among the step's candidates (guardrail; controller.SEARCH_BY)
